🇺🇸🇷🇺🇨🇳 US Continues Developing INF Treaty-Violating Ground Launch Systems for Cruise Missiles... 

A recent article by Naval News (link below) talks about a new selection of potential mobile launchers for larger, long-range missiles including the Tomahawk cruise missile. 

There is no fundamental technical obstacle for doing this. 

The Typhon was seen as unsatisfactory by the US Army for its cumbersome profile - although the US Army is already deploying it but is considering the already tested Long Range Fires Launcher the US Marines were testing, to compliment the Typhon for greater mobility.

The US Army plans to test fire the LRF Launcher as early as next year in the Philippines meaning there is really no additional work required - they are just timing it for scheduled exercises next year.

You just need a large, stable truck to attach the system to and you have a mobile launcher.

Russia has loads of them and there is no real reason the US doesn't yet except the typical corruption and paralysis profit over purpose creates.

The article is here: https://t.co/RkmgFfQ216

These newer systems will need to be fully tested - and it might take a year or 2 - in the meantime they will have functioning Typhon systems and likely LRF Launchers on hand in the interim.

If Tomahawks are deployed to Ukraine the LRF Launcher is a likely candidate - or maybe some adhoc stripped down trailer-truck mounted version of the Typhon with fewer Mk 41 VLS cells which served as prototypes for the Typhon and LRF Launchers.  

The real bottleneck is and will continue to be Tomahawk missile production which is under 100 per year vs. 300-600 Russian Kalibr cruise missiles per year (and growing). 

h/t @DagnyTaggart963
